explanation: The I84V mutation reduces darunavir binding through loss of favorable van der Waals contacts in the S2/S2' subpocket. Isoleucine's branched side chain at position 84 creates more extensive hydrophobic packing interactions with darunavir's ligand surface; substitution to the smaller valine removes ~27 Ų of contact surface area, creating a cavity that weakens the energetic contribution of this interaction despite the 4.1 Å proximity. This localized binding pocket deterioration is modest (negative ΔΔG of only 0.14 kcal/mol) because darunavir likely maintains compensatory interactions elsewhere, but the cumulative effect of reduced hydrophobic complementarity is sufficient to provide selective resistance.
